answer: Give each identity a sonnet: fourteen linked lines, each signed by a distinct sponsor, hashing the line before, so it rhymes only if the chain is genuine. A sponsor's stake lies frozen in tundra, thawing one line per epoch, capping endorsements; the Nth clone costs more as thaw slots shrink. Each epoch a raven challenges a random identity with a memory-hard sequential proof salted by address, unprecomputable in parallel. If one identity fails, its sonnet collapses and all sponsors on that chain are slashed together, so N clones sharing sponsors risk about N squared in forfeited stake.
